findings: Small spec/checker/test target; no new dependency and no new oya CLI surface.
Coverage target shape requires Buck2 ownership, Build ID evidence, profile sharding, report paths, changed-file delta, and generated-code exclusions.
RED mutations cover missing instrumentation, profile collision guard loss, tool loss, Tarpaulin boundary loss, and false coverage-report claims.
Contract records the runner shape before forcing teams to adopt a live coverage lane.
Checker is deterministic Python and target is reachable through Buck2.
Rejected Tarpaulin and ad-hoc local reports as merge authority; rejected claiming a report before one is generated.
No secrets, branch protection mutation, or tenant data touched.
Contract target is wired into the existing Buck2 authority policy chain.
No new oya CLI surface; cloud-ci/oya-ci oya-ci-required remains destination authority; contract output is local/static evidence only.
Automatable coverage-runner shape is mapped to a Buck2 target and policy anchors.
Machine-readable spec plus existing testing standard pointer avoids root doc sprawl.
